why: THREE STATES, AND ALL THREE EXIST BECAUSE THIS UNIT'S STATE MACHINE HAS AN
ENTRY STATE THE GENERATED CORPUS NEVER PRODUCES. The first sweep scored 58
of 83 and an arm census -- the shipped translation plus counters, run
through the same harness, evidence/YawRateControl/arm_census.txt -- says
exactly where the 25 survivors live:
calls 8036 | Y_ControlMode == 1  961 | iStatus == 0 init 240
ENTRY YawState:   1 -> 0     -1 -> 719     0 -> 242
from  0: start-right-only 0   start-left-only 48   BOTH ifs 192
`YawState` IS NEVER 1 ON ENTRY, IN 8036 CASES, and the reason is arithmetic
rather than luck. The third arm's two `IF`s are independent, so a NEGATIVE
`deadband` makes both fire and the second write wins:
IF (NacHeadingError .gt.  deadband) YawState =  1
IF (NacHeadingError .lt. -deadband) YawState = -1
R6 draws `Y_ErrThresh` on the +/-1e3 default, so `deadband` is negative in
192 of the 242 cases that reach the third arm and -1 wins every one of
them; in the other 48 only the left test fires. Zero cases leave the arm at
+1, so the whole `YawState == 1` block -- four statements and three
predicates -- is dead in the corpus.
THE STATES BELOW MAKE `deadband` SMALL AND NON-NEGATIVE AND THE ERROR
POSITIVE, which is the only shape that reaches `start-right-only`. The next
case in the block then ENTERS at +1, because the harness advances this
unit's SAVE state by calling it -- state is not a parameter here and no case
can set it directly.
REACHING A CONTROLLED `NacHeadingError` AT ALL IS UNIT #41's ROUTE, MET FOR
THE THIRD TIME. The error is a filtered quantity:
WindDirPlusOffsetCosF = LPFilter(cos(WindDirPlusOffset*D2R), ..., F_YawErr, ...)
NacHeadingTarget      = wrap_180(atan2(SinF, CosF) * R2D)
NacHeadingError       = wrap_180(NacHeadingTarget - NacHeading)
and `LPFilter`'s initialisation arm returns its input BIT-EXACTLY at
`CornerFreq = 0`: the coefficients become 2, -2, 0, 0 and the expression
collapses to `(1/2)*(2x)`, both operations exact. So `F_YawErr = 0` with
`iStatus = 0` turns the two filtered components back into `cos` and `sin` of
the input, `atan2` inverts them, and `NacHeadingError` is the wind direction
the case states -- to within the `D2R * R2D` round trip, which is 1e-11 and
which none of these states depends on being exact except state C, where the
input is 0 and every step is exact.
WHAT NO STATE IN THIS FILE CAN REACH, stated here rather than left to the
score. Entering the `YawState == 1` or `YawState == -1` arm requires
`iStatus /= 0`, because `iStatus == 0` resets `YawState` to 0 two statements
earlier. But `LocalVar%FP` is zero-initialised by the harness on EVERY case
and is not varied, so at `iStatus /= 0` LPFilter takes its steady-state arm
with a1 = a0 = b1 = b0 = 0 and returns
Every comparison against NaN is false, so both stop arms -- `error <= 0`
inside the right arm and `error >= 0` inside the left -- are UNREACHABLE by
construction, and the census agrees: 719 entries at -1 and `stop 0` on all
of them. That is a property of the instrument, not of the reference: in the
shipped program `FP` persists across calls and both stops fire, twelve and
eleven times respectively in scenario 7. The kernel is the layer that sees
them, and evidence/YawRateControl/kernel.stubs.txt is where that is
measured.
`Y_ErrThresh` IS A RAMP FROM 0 rather than a fill, for R5's reason and for a
second one: the two elements are what the `WE_Vw_F <= Y_uSwitch` test
chooses between, so with them equal that predicate and both of its
subscripts are unkillable. The ramp is [0, 1, 2, 3, ...], which puts
element 1 at 0 -- the value state C needs for an EQUALITY against an error
of exactly 0 -- and keeps every neighbouring index a different number.
`WE_Vw_F` AND `Y_uSwitch` ARE BOTH 0, i.e. AT EQUALITY. R6 already names
them a relational pair and generates the equality and its two neighbours
from whatever base the case carries; setting the base to equality as well
means the states' own cases sit on the boundary rather than beside it.
`OL_Mode = 0` in all three, so the open-loop override never fires from a
state. R6's own knob moves `OL_Mode` and `Ind_YawRate` to 1 and 2 from each
state, which is what puts the override under a controlled error instead of
under the +/-1e3 draw; `OL_Breakpoints` ramps strictly increasing so
`interp1d` raises no error, and `OL_YawRate` ramps with a different step so
a wrong array or a wrong length gives a different interpolant.
FOUR STATES ADDED 2026-08-15, AND THEY ARE A SEQUENCE RATHER THAN FOUR
INDEPENDENT SHAPES. They exist to reach the two STOP arms, which the
paragraph above records as unreachable -- correctly, for the corpus as it
then was. What changed is not the record but the INPUT: `LocalVar%FP` is now
carried from case to case (`vit_harness.py --persist-nested LocalVar.FP`)
instead of being zeroed on every one. All-zero filter coefficients at
`iStatus /= 0` are not a value any reachable program state produces -- the
shipped program initialises FP on the first call and reads it on every call
after -- and feeding them to the reference put LPFilter's own arithmetic on
1.0/0 and made both stop arms dead by construction.
The four run in order and each depends on the one before it:
start_right ... -> leaves YawState = +1 on EVERY case of its block
stop_right  ... -> enters at +1, error exactly 0, takes `.le. 0`
start_left  ... -> leaves YawState = -1 on EVERY case of its block
stop_left   ... -> enters at -1, error exactly 0, takes `.ge. 0`
THE ARITHMETIC THAT MAKES THE ERROR EXACTLY ZERO, rather than 1e-11 from it.
`NacHeading + NacVane = 0` exactly in every one of the four, so
`WindDirPlusOffset` is 0 and the two filter inputs are cos(0) = 1.0 and
sin(0) = 0.0 -- both exact, both preserved by an identity filter, and
`atan2(0.0, 1.0)` is 0.0. The D2R/R2D round trip that costs state A its last
eleven digits never runs on a non-zero angle here. `ZMQ_YawOffset` is pinned
to 0 so the `ZMQ_Mode = 1` knob cannot move the angle off zero inside a
block, and `objInst_instLPF` is pinned so that the FP slot one state writes
is the slot the next one reads.

states.name: start_right_at_a_small_positive_error
states.why: The state that makes YawState = 1, which nothing else in the corpus does. F_YawErr = 0 with iStatus = 0 makes both LPFilter calls the identity, so NacHeadingError is 0.5 degrees; WE_Vw_F = Y_uSwitch = 0 takes the low-wind arm, whose Y_ErrThresh(1) is 0; 0.5 > 0 fires the right test and 0.5 < -0 does not fire the left, so the arm leaves YawState at +1 and the next case in the block enters the YawState == 1 arm. The error sits strictly between Y_ErrThresh(1) = 0 and Y_ErrThresh(2) = 1, so switching the deadband -- by the WE_Vw_F test, by either subscript, or by an index mutant -- changes the answer and is visible in DebugVar%YawState on the same case. NacVane is the only non-zero of the two wind-direction terms, so a sign flip on NacHeading + NacVane moves LocalVar%WindDir, which is compared.

states.name: start_right_above_the_second_threshold
states.why: The same shape at an error of 2 degrees, which is above Y_ErrThresh(2) = 1 and below Y_ErrThresh(4) = 3. It is what distinguishes the HIGH-wind deadband from an index one past it: at WE_Vw_F > Y_uSwitch the reference reads element 2 and 2 > 1 fires the right test, while an index mutant reading element 4 gets 3 and nothing fires. WE_Vw_F is 1 against Y_uSwitch 0 so this state takes the else arm of the wind test, which state A does not.

states.name: error_exactly_at_a_zero_deadband
states.why: The EQUALITY, and the only state in which every step of the computation is exact. Every wind-direction term is 0, so WindDirPlusOffset is 0, cos is 1, sin is 0, both LPFilter calls are the identity at F_YawErr = 0, atan2(0, 1) is 0, wrap_180(0) is 0 and NacHeadingError is exactly 0.0. Y_ErrThresh(1) is exactly 0.0 and the low-wind arm is taken, so the third arm tests 0 > 0 and 0 < -0: the reference fires neither and leaves YawState at 0, while `>` widened to `>=` leaves it at +1 and `<` widened to `<=` leaves it at -1. Both differences reach DebugVar%YawState on the same case, so this state kills the two strictness mutants that no ladder over a computed quantity can reach.

states.name: start_right_with_the_wind_direction_at_zero
states.why: START RIGHT WITH THE WIND DIRECTION AT EXACTLY ZERO -- the first of the two states that set up an EXACTLY-ZERO yaw error one case later, which is the only input on which `NacHeadingError .le. 0` and `.lt. 0` give different answers. `NacHeading + NacVane = 0` EXACTLY (-0.5 + 0.5 in binary), so `WindDirPlusOffset` is 0 whatever this block's R11 knob does to `ZMQ_Mode` (`LocalVar%ZMQ_YawOffset` is pinned to 0 here for that reason) and both LPFilter inputs are cos(0) = 1.0 and sin(0) = 0.0, both exact. `F_YawErr = 0` makes the filter the identity at `iStatus == 0` (a1 = 2, a0 = -2, b1 = b0 = 0, so 1/2 * (2x) = x) and a FIXED POINT afterwards (result = OutputSignalLast, which is then stored back unchanged) -- so with `--persist-nested LocalVar.FP` the pair (1.0, 0.0) survives every later case in this block and the next, and `NacHeadingTarget = wrap_180(atan2(0.0, 1.0) * R2D)` is 0.0 exactly. `objInst_instLPF` is pinned so the slot the next state READS is the slot this state WRITES; unpinned it is drawn per case and the carry lands somewhere else. The error is then `wrap_180(0 - NacHeading)` = 0.5, above the `Y_ErrThresh(1) = 0` deadband, so this state leaves `YawState = +1` -- and so does every case in its block, whichever knob moved: `iStatus = 0` resets and re-starts, `Y_ControlMode /= 1` skips the body, and the rest persist at 0.5.

states.name: stop_right_at_an_exactly_zero_error
states.why: STOP RIGHT AT AN EXACTLY ZERO ERROR. Enters at `YawState = +1` (the previous state's block leaves it there on every case) with `iStatus = 1`, so the reset does not fire and the carried `LocalVar%FP` -- frozen at (1.0, 0.0) by the previous state -- gives `NacHeadingTarget = 0.0` exactly; `NacHeading = 0` makes `NacHeadingError` 0.0 exactly. `0 .le. 0` is TRUE and `0 .lt. 0` is FALSE, so this is the case that separates them: the reference stops (`YawRateCom = 0`, `YawState = 0`) and the `<` mutant persists at `Y_Rate = 4`. It is also where `YawRateCom = 0.0 -> 1.0` and `YawState = 0 -> 1` first execute. WITHOUT the carried FP this case is unreachable: at `iStatus /= 0` a zero-initialised FP makes LPFilter evaluate 1.0/0 * 0 = NaN, every comparison against it false, and both stop arms dead -- which is what the first sweep's eight survivors were.

states.name: start_left_with_the_wind_direction_at_zero
states.why: START LEFT WITH THE WIND DIRECTION AT EXACTLY ZERO. The mirror of `start_right_with_the_wind_direction_at_zero`, and it re-establishes the same frozen (1.0, 0.0) filter state at `iStatus = 0` so the stop-left state after it does not depend on what the intervening block did. `NacHeading = +0.5` with `NacVane = -0.5` gives an error of -0.5: `-0.5 .gt. 0` is false and `-0.5 .lt. -0` is true, so the third arm's SECOND `IF` fires and the block leaves `YawState = -1`.

states.name: stop_left_at_an_exactly_zero_error
states.why: STOP LEFT AT AN EXACTLY ZERO ERROR. Enters at `YawState = -1` with the carried FP frozen at (1.0, 0.0), so `NacHeadingError` is 0.0 exactly. `0 .ge. 0` is TRUE, `0 .gt. 0` is FALSE and `0 .ge. 1` is FALSE -- one case separating the reference from the `>` mutant AND from the `0.0 -> 1.0` constant on the same comparison, which no non-zero error can do (at an error of -0.5 all three are false together).
